subject: Routing policy lab: confirm POC kickoff + hands-on and load-test window
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Su <elena.su@acme-retail.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Routing policy lab: proposed kickoff + hands-on windows and prework

Hi Elena / Daniel —

Thanks again for agreeing to run the routing-policy POC with us. To keep the scope tight (prompt review, model selection + fallback rules, regional tiering, and a short load run), we propose the following plan and a pair of calendar blocks during the week of March 8: 

- Kickoff (30 min): context, success criteria, stakeholders, scoring rubric
- Hands-on lab (2 hours): prompt walkthrough, model selection exercise, configure fallback rules, small-scale load runs in staging
- Post-lab next steps: rollback/roll-forward plan and measurement checklist

Proposed windows (all PT):
- Option A: Wed, Mar 10 — Kickoff 10:00–10:30, Hands-on 10:45–12:45
- Option B: Thu, Mar 11 — Kickoff 09:00–09:30, Hands-on 09:45–11:45

Can you confirm which option works better and who from your side will attend the hands-on (devs + infra ideally)?

Prework we need from Acme by March 5:
- Sample prompt set (10–20 prompts representative of peak and tail traffic)
- Traffic profile (tokens/sec, concurrency, typical sequence lengths)
- Any IP/egress rules or sandbox constraints (so our infra team can whitelist)

I attached a short POC-Overview.pdf and a suggested loadtest-plan.xlsx. If either window conflicts with your security review, let us know and we can move the hands-on later in the week.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

A few notes from our side:
- Daniel (cc) will be the primary contact for run-of-show and verification of traffic profiles.
- Please add Sam Wilson (sam.wilson@acme-retail.com) — he is our staging infra owner and will need the staging endpoints whitelisted.

Thanks Elena — we can do that. Confirming schedule and logistics: 

Wed, Mar 10 (PT) — UPDATED TIMES
- 10:00–10:30 Kickoff (high-level goals & success criteria)
- 10:30–13:00 Hands-on lab (lab start moved 30m to accommodate Acme)

Attendees (Redwood): Logan, Marissa (facilitator), Ben (solutions), Markus (runtime engineer), Naomi (customer success)
Expected Attendees (Acme): Elena (product), Daniel (tech lead), Sam (staging infra) + 1 dev (optional)

Prework checklist for Acme (due Mar 5):
- Prompt set (10–20 examples) — place in shared Drive link or paste into the HubSpot deal
- Traffic profile (CSV): concurrency, p50/p95 seq len, expected burst sizes
- IPs to whitelist (Sam will confirm)

Model shortlist we'll exercise in the lab (for planning, we can expand if you have preferences):
- redwood-mini-13b-int8 (fast, lower cost)
- llama-3-70b-q4 (higher quality for long-context prompts)

Fallback & tiering topics to cover: regional fallback, degraded-quality tier, and automatic fallback to warm cached responses for identified prefixes. We'll bring templates for policy snippets.

Load-run plan: brief 15–30 minute ramp to validate routing and cache behavior. Full-scale soak can be scheduled afterwards once config is finalized.

Calendar invite has been created: https://calendar.redwood.com/event/5f3a2c-routing-lab-march-10 — please accept and add Sam to the invite.

If Acme requires SOC2 evidence ahead of the session, we can provide the redacted report and retention doc; we'll put links in the invite once you confirm.

— Marissa

On the SOC2 evidence: happy to accept a redacted copy; we'll treat it per our vendor onboarding process. For the short load run, please ensure that test traffic is clearly tagged (test_run=true) so it does not affect our monitoring dashboards.

We will upload the prompt set and traffic CSV to the HubSpot deal record (ACME-2952) by EOD Mar 5. See you on Mar 10.

— Daniel
